`documents` table includes columns: `id` (UUID PK), `status` (enum), `content_hash` (unique), `storage_key`, `original_filename`, `mime_type`, `document_type_id` (FK), `uploaded_by` (FK), `created_at`, `updated_at` - `status` column uses PostgreSQL enum with values: `Caricato`, `In elaborazione`, `Da validare`, `Validato`, `Rifiutato`, `Archiviato`, `Errore` - `validation_tasks` table includes: `id`, `document_id` (FK), `status` (enum: `Aperto`, `Assegnato`, `Completato`, `Annullato`), `assigned_to`, `created_at`, `completed_at`, `outcome`, `notes` - `export_jobs` table includes: `id`, `requested_by`, `status` (enum: `Pending`, `Processing`, `Completed`, `Failed`), `filter_criteria` (JSONB), `output_key`, `created_at`, `completed_at` - `audit_log` table includes: `id`, `actor_id`, `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `detail` (JSONB), `created_at` — append-only, no UPDATE or DELETE allowed - `vector_chunks` table includes: `id`, `document_id` (FK), `chunk_index`, `content_text`, `embedding` (vector type via pgvector), `created_at` - All tables include `created_at` and `updated_at` (where mutable) with server-default timestamps - Foreign key constraints enforce referential integrity between documents, tasks, exports, and audit - A CHECK constraint or application-level invariant ensures `vector_chunks` rows reference only documents with `status = 'Validato'` - Migration is idempotent: running it twice produces no errors and no duplicate objects - SQLAlchemy ORM models in `src/backend/db/models/` map 1:1 to the migration tables and are importable by all downstream REQs - Seed data script creates at least one document type for integration testing ### Acceptance — REQ-002 - Python abstract base classes define adapter interfaces: `ObjectStorageAdapter`, `QueueAdapter`, `EventAdapter`, `SecretAdapter` - `ObjectStorageAdapter` exposes: `put_object(key, data, metadata)`, `get_object(key)`, `delete_object(key)`, `generate_presigned_url(key, expiry)` - `QueueAdapter` exposes: `send_message(queue_name, payload)`, `receive_messages(queue_name, max_count, wait_seconds)`, `delete_message(queue_name, receipt_handle)` - `EventAdapter` exposes: `publish(topic, event_type, payload)` - `SecretAdapter` exposes: `get_secret(name)` returning string value - AWS implementations: `S3StorageAdapter`, `SQSQueueAdapter`, `SNSEventAdapter`, `SecretsManagerAdapter` - Profile selection driven by `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE` environment variable (`aws` or `onprem`) - A `get_adapter(interface_type)` factory function returns the correct implementation based on active profile - On-prem adapter stubs raise `NotImplementedError` with clear message (implementation deferred) - Integration tests use localstack or moto to verify AWS adapter behavior for put/get/delete/presign on S3 and send/receive/delete on SQS - Configuration module at `src/backend/shared/config.py` loads profile and adapter settings from environment with Pydantic Settings - No business logic in adapter modules; adapters are pure infrastructure wrappers - All adapters are async-compatible (async def methods) ### Acceptance — REQ-003 - OIDC JWT validation middleware extracts and verifies tokens from `Authorization: Bearer` header - Token validation checks: signature (via JWKS), expiration, issuer, audience - Roles extracted from configurable JWT claim path (default `realm_access.roles` for Keycloak compatibility) - RBAC decorator `@require_roles(*roles)` applicable to any FastAPI route; returns 403 with JSON error body when role missing - Predefined roles: `operator`, `validator`, `admin`, `viewer`, `service` - Anonymous requests (no token) receive 401 with JSON error body - Expired or malformed tokens receive 401 with JSON error body - Current user context (`CurrentUser` dataclass with `user_id`, `email`, `roles`, `raw_claims`) injectable via FastAPI dependency - JWKS endpoint URL and issuer configurable via environment variables - JWKS keys cached with configurable TTL (default 3600s) to avoid per-request fetch - Reuses and extends existing `src/backend/shared/authz/` module; does not create parallel auth module - Unit tests cover: valid token → 200, expired token → 401, missing token → 401, wrong role → 403, valid role → 200 - Integration test with a mock OIDC provider verifies full middleware chain ### Acceptance — REQ-004 - `AuditService` class with method `log(actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, detail)` persists to `audit_log` table - All audit writes are append-only; service never issues UPDATE or DELETE on `audit_log` - PII fields in `detail` JSONB are redacted before persistence using a configurable redaction list (default: `email`, `name`, `address`, `phone`) - Audit records include server-generated `created_at` timestamp (not client-supplied) - `actor_id` is extracted from `CurrentUser` context; system/service actions use a well-known service actor ID - Audit service is injectable as a FastAPI dependency for use by all downstream REQs - Query endpoint `GET /api/v1/audit` returns paginated audit records filtered by `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `actor_id`, `action`, `date_range`; requires `admin` role - Non-admin roles receive 403 when querying audit endpoint - Unit tests verify: record creation, PII redaction, append-only enforcement (mock DB rejects UPDATE) - Integration test verifies round-trip: log an action → query it back → verify all fields present and PII redacted ### Acceptance — REQ-005 - `POST /api/v1/documents/upload` accepts multipart file upload with metadata fields (`document_type`, `tags`, `description`) - Supported MIME types: `application/pdf`, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.*`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`; unsupported types return 415 - File stored in object storage via `ObjectStorageAdapter.put_object` with key pattern `uploads/{document_id}/{original_filename}` - SHA-256 content hash computed; if hash already exists in `documents` table, return 409 Conflict with reference to existing document - New `documents` row created with `status = 'Caricato'`, `content_hash`, `storage_key`, `original_filename`, `mime_type`, `uploaded_by` - Processing message published to queue via `QueueAdapter.send_message` with payload `{document_id, storage_key, mime_type}` - Audit record created: action `document.uploaded`, entity `document`, detail includes filename and size - Requires `operator` or `admin` role; other roles receive 403 - Anonymous requests receive 401 - Response returns 201 with document ID, status, and storage key - File size limit enforced (configurable, default 100MB); oversized uploads return 413 - Unit tests: successful upload, duplicate hash rejection, unsupported MIME type, oversized file, missing auth, wrong role - Integration test: upload file → verify DB record → verify object in storage → verify queue message published → verify audit record ### Acceptance — REQ-006 - Queue consumer listens on document processing queue and processes messages containing `{document_id, storage_key, mime_type}` - Document status transitions from `Caricato` to `In elaborazione` at processing start; transition recorded via audit - OCR performed using Tesseract on image-based documents (PDF images, JPG, PNG); extracted text stored in `document_metadata` or `documents.extracted_text` - Text parsing performed using Apache Tika for text-based documents (PDF text, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) - Rule-based classification assigns `document_type_id` based on configurable keyword/pattern rules (e.g., "invoice" if contains "fattura" or "invoice number") - On success: document status transitions to `Da validare`; audit record created with action `document.processed` - On failure (OCR error, parsing error, unrecoverable): document status transitions to `Errore`; audit record created with action `document.processing_failed` including error detail - Processing is idempotent: reprocessing same message does not create duplicate metadata or corrupt state - Message acknowledged (deleted from queue) only after successful state transition - Failed messages remain on queue for retry up to configurable max attempts (default 3); after max retries, moved to dead-letter or marked `Errore` - Unit tests: successful OCR + parse + classify, OCR failure → Errore, idempotent reprocessing, classification rule matching - Integration test: place message on queue → consumer processes → verify DB state `Da validare` → verify extracted text stored → verify audit records ### Acceptance — REQ-007 - `DocumentLifecycleService` enforces a state machine with allowed transitions: - `Caricato` → `In elaborazione` - `In elaborazione` → `Da validare`, `Errore` - `Da validare` → `Validato`, `Rifiutato` - `Rifiutato` → `Da validare` (resubmit for re-validation) - `Validato` → `Archiviato` - `Errore` → `Caricato` (retry) - All other transitions are forbidden and raise `InvalidTransitionError` (HTTP 409) - Every successful transition persists: new status on `documents` row, audit record with `action = 'document.state_changed'`, `detail` includes `from_state`, `to_state`, `reason` - `GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/transitions` returns ordered history of all state transitions for the document - `POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/transition` accepts `{target_state, reason}` and executes transition if allowed - Transition API requires `operator`, `validator`, or `admin` role depending on transition type (validator required for `Da validare` → `Validato`/`Rifiutato`) - Concurrent transition attempts on same document handled via optimistic locking (version column or SELECT FOR UPDATE); second attempt returns 409 - Unit tests: every valid transition, every forbidden transition, concurrent conflict, audit record creation - Integration test: walk a document through full lifecycle `Caricato` → `In elaborazione` → `Da validare` → `Validato` → `Archiviato` verifying state and audit at each step ### Acceptance — REQ-008 - When a document transitions to `Da validare`, a `validation_tasks` row is automatically created with `status = 'Aperto'` and `document_id` FK - `GET /api/v1/tasks` returns paginated task list; filterable by `status`, `document_type`, `assigned_to`, `created_after`, `created_before` - `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/claim` assigns task to current user; transitions task status from `Aperto` to `Assegnato`; returns 409 if already assigned - `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/release` returns task to `Aperto` pool; only current assignee or admin can release - Task detail includes: document summary (type, filename, upload date), current document status, extracted text preview - Requires `validator` or `admin` role for claim/release; `viewer` can list but not claim - Audit record created for task creation, claim, and release actions - When document transitions away from `Da validare` (e.g., to `Errore` via admin override), associated open tasks are cancelled (`status = 'Annullato'`) - Unit tests: auto-creation on state change, claim success, claim conflict, release by non-assignee denied, task cancellation on document state change - Integration test: upload + process document → verify task created → claim task → verify assignment → release → verify back to open ### Acceptance — REQ-009 - `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/approve` transitions document to `Validato` and task to `Completato` with `outcome = 'approved'` - `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/reject` transitions document to `Rifiutato` and task to `Completato` with `outcome = 'rejected'`; `notes` field mandatory (400 if missing) - Both endpoints require `validator` or `admin` role; `operator` role receives 403 - Task must be in `Assegnato` status and assigned to current user (or admin override); otherwise 409 - Document transition uses `DocumentLifecycleService` ensuring state machine rules are enforced - Approval triggers event `document.validated` via `EventAdapter.publish` for downstream consumers (indexing, archival) - Rejection triggers event `document.rejected` via `EventAdapter.publish` - Audit records created for both approval and rejection with actor, outcome, and notes - After rejection, document can be resubmitted: `Rifiutato` → `Da validare` creates a new task (previous task remains `Completato`) - Unit tests: approve happy path, reject with notes, reject without notes → 400, wrong role → 403, task not assigned to actor → 409, event publication verified - Integration test: full flow from task claim → approve → verify document `Validato` → verify event published → verify audit ### Acceptance — REQ-010 - `GET /api/v1/archive/search` accepts query parameters: `q` (full-text), `document_type`, `status`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `tags`, `page`, `page_size` - Full-text search uses PostgreSQL `tsvector`/`tsquery` over extracted document content - Results include: document ID, title/filename, document type, status, relevance score, created date, snippet/highlight - Results paginated with `page`, `page_size` (default 20, max 100), total count in response - Only documents with status `Validato` or `Archiviato` appear in archive search results (other statuses excluded) - Requires `operator`, `validator`, `admin`, or `viewer` role; anonymous receives 401 - Empty query with filters returns filtered results ordered by date descending - Audit record created for each search query with actor and query parameters (search terms redacted if containing PII patterns) - Performance: search returns within 500ms for up to 100k documents (index required on tsvector column) - Unit tests: full-text match, metadata filter, combined query + filter, status exclusion, pagination boundary, empty results - Integration test: insert test documents with various statuses → search → verify only Validato/Archiviato returned → verify pagination → verify audit ### Acceptance — REQ-011 - `POST /api/v1/archive/export` accepts `{filter_criteria, format}` where `filter_criteria` matches search filters and `format` is `zip` or `pdf-bundle` - Export restricted to documents with status `Validato` or `Archiviato`; request including other statuses returns 400 - Creates `export_jobs` row with `status = 'Pending'` and queues processing message - Async worker processes export: collects matching documents from object storage, packages into requested format, uploads result to object storage - Export job transitions: `Pending` → `Processing` → `Completed` or `Failed` - `GET /api/v1/archive/export/{job_id}` returns job status; when `Completed`, includes presigned download URL (expiry configurable, default 1 hour) - `GET /api/v1/archive/export` lists current user's export jobs with status and creation date - Requires `operator` or `admin` role; `viewer` receives 403 - Audit records created for export request and export completion/failure - Export job that references zero matching documents returns 400 immediately without creating a job - Unit tests: job creation, status polling, zero-match rejection, role enforcement, presigned URL generation - Integration test: create export → poll until completed → download via presigned URL → verify archive contents match filter ### Acceptance — REQ-012 - When a document transitions to `Validato`, an indexing job is triggered (via event listener on `document.validated`) - Document content chunked using configurable strategy (default: 512-token sliding window with 64-token overlap) - Each chunk embedded using bge-m3 model; embedding stored in `vector_chunks` table with `document_id`, `chunk_index`, `content_text`, `embedding` - Only documents with `status = 'Validato'` are indexed; indexing request for non-validated document is rejected and logged - If document transitions away from `Validato` (e.g., admin reverts), associated `vector_chunks` rows are deleted - Indexing is idempotent: re-indexing same document replaces existing chunks (delete + insert within transaction) - `GET /api/v1/ai/index/status/{document_id}` returns indexing status: `not_indexed`, `indexing`, `indexed`, `error` - Requires `admin` or `service` role for manual index trigger; automatic indexing uses service identity - Audit record created for indexing start and completion - Unit tests: chunk generation, embedding dimension validation, idempotent re-index, non-validated rejection, chunk deletion on state revert - Integration test: validate document → verify chunks created in pgvector → query by similarity → verify results ### Acceptance — REQ-013 - `POST /api/v1/ai/query` accepts `{question, filters, max_results}` and returns `{answer, sources, confidence}` - Retrieval: query embedded with bge-m3, top-K chunks retrieved from pgvector using cosine similarity (default K=20) - Reranking: retrieved chunks reranked using bge-reranker; top-N passed to LLM (default N=5) - Generation: LLM (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct or Mistral-7B-Instruct per config) generates answer with source attribution - Only chunks from `Validato` documents included in retrieval (enforced by JOIN on document status) - Response includes: generated answer, list of source documents (ID, title, chunk snippet, relevance score), confidence indicator - Prompt logging disabled; query and response metadata logged without PII or business content (redaction enforced) - Requires `operator`, `validator`, or `admin` role; `viewer` can query but results limited to document titles only (no content) - Anonymous requests receive 401 - If no relevant chunks found, returns empty answer with `confidence = 'none'` and empty sources - Latency target: response within 5 seconds for typical queries (excluding cold-start) - Audit record created for each query with actor, query hash (not raw query), result count - Unit tests: retrieval with mock pgvector, reranking order verification, validated-only filter, empty results, role-based response filtering, PII redaction in logs - Integration test: index validated documents → query → verify answer references only validated sources → verify audit ### Acceptance — REQ-014 - Single `FastAPI` application in `src/backend/app.py` mounts all domain routers: documents, workflow, archive, AI, audit, health - `GET /health` returns `{"status": "ok"}` with 200 when all dependencies reachable - `GET /ready` returns 200 when database connection pool active and queue adapter connected; 503 otherwise - OpenAPI spec auto-generated at `/docs` and `/openapi.json`; includes all mounted routes with request/response schemas - CORS middleware configured with allowed origins from environment variable - Global exception handlers return consistent JSON error format: `{"error": "code", "message": "human-readable", "detail": {}}` - document processing, workflow orchestration, AI/RAG pipeline, and shared infrastructure adapters. Used by REQs in the `backend`, `ai-rag`, and `infra` lanes defined in TECH_CONSTRAINTS. ### REQ Usage Rules - All backend App-track REQs (REQ-002 through REQ-014) use this lane - REQs producing API endpoints must emit router, service, schema, and test files - REQs producing async consumers must emit consumer, handler, and integration test files - When a REQ depends on adapters (REQ-002), it must import from `backend.shared.adapters`, not create local adapter code - When a REQ depends on auth (REQ-003), it must use `@require_roles` and `CurrentUser` from `backend.shared.authz` - When a REQ depends on audit (REQ-004), it must inject `AuditService` from `backend.shared.audit` - This lane alone is insufficient for frontend REQs; those use `js-ts` lane ### Tools - **tests:** pytest 8.x + pytest-asyncio + pytest-cov + httpx (TestClient) + factory_boy + moto (AWS mocks) + testcontainers-python (PostgreSQL + pgvector) - **lint:** ruff (replaces flake8 + isort + black) - **types:** mypy with strict mode or pyright - **security:** bandit + safety (dependency audit) + Trivy (container scan) - **build:** pip-tools or poetry for dependency lock; Docker multi-stage build ### Artifacts Expected - `runs/kit//src/` — production source files - `runs/kit//test/` — test files (unit + integration) - `runs/kit//test/api/` — `.http` files for API endpoint REQs (curl-compatible) - `runs/kit//reports/coverage.xml` — pytest-cov XML report - `runs/kit//reports/lint.txt` — ruff output - `runs/kit//reports/types.txt` — mypy output - `runs/kit//reports/security.txt` — bandit output - `/eval` normalizes: coverage percentage, lint error count, type error count, critical vulnerability count ### CLI Examples - **Local:** - `pytest test/backend/ --cov=src/backend --cov-report=xml:reports/coverage.xml -v` - `ruff check src/backend/ > reports/lint.txt` - `mypy src/backend/ > reports/types.txt` - `bandit -r src/backend/ -f txt > reports/security.txt` - **Containerized:** - `docker compose run --rm backend pytest --cov --cov-report=xml` - `docker compose run --rm backend ruff check .` ### Default Gate Policy - **min coverage:** 80% - **max criticals:** 0 (bandit HIGH + Trivy CRITICAL) - **lint must be clean:** yes (ruff exit code 0) - **type errors:** 0 (mypy strict) - **fail conditions:** any of the above thresholds breached; any integration test failure; missing mandatory test categories per REQ ### Lane-Specific Failure Modes - **Missing async test fixtures:** pytest-asyncio requires `@pytest.mark.asyncio` and proper event loop scope; omitting causes silent skips - **moto mock scope:** moto decorators must wrap the entire test function or class; partial mocking causes real AWS calls - **testcontainers port conflicts:** parallel CI runs may collide on PostgreSQL ports; use random port allocation - **pgvector extension missing:** testcontainers PostgreSQL image must include pgvector; use `ankane/pgvector` image - **Pydantic v2 migration:** all models must use Pydantic v2 syntax (`model_validator`, `field_validator`); v1 compat mode forbidden - **SQLAlchemy 2.0 style:** use `select()` statements, not legacy `Query` API - **FastAPI dependency injection:** test overrides must use `app.dependency_overrides`, not monkeypatching ### Enterprise Runner Notes - **SonarQube:** import `coverage.xml` as Python coverage report; import `ruff` output as external issue report - **GitHub Actions:** use `actions/setup-python@v5` with Python 3.12; cache pip dependencies; run testcontainers via Docker-in-Docker or service containers - **Artifact fetch:** coverage and lint reports at `runs/kit//reports/` ### TECH_CONSTRAINTS Integration - **Air-gap:** all pip packages must be available from approved internal PyPI mirror; no runtime downloads - **Registries:** Docker images from approved internal registry; base image `python:3.12-slim` - **Tokens and secrets:** never hardcode; use `SecretAdapter` from REQ-002; test secrets via environment variables in CI - **GDPR:** PII redaction via REQ-004 audit service; Used by REQ-001 (data backbone) and referenced by all downstream REQs that read or write to PostgreSQL. ### REQ Usage Rules - REQ-001 is the primary REQ using this lane directly - All other REQs that interact with the database import ORM models from `backend.db.models` but do not create new migrations (unless explicitly authorized) - Schema changes after REQ-001 require a new migration file in the same Alembic chain - This lane must be combined with `python` lane when the REQ also includes application logic ### Tools - **tests:** pytest + testcontainers-python (PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector) for migration verification - **lint:** sqlfluff for SQL file linting (if raw SQL files exist) - **types:** N/A (schema validated by migration execution) - **security:** no direct security tooling; schema-level constraints (FK, CHECK, enum) are the security layer - **build:** Alembic `upgrade head` as build verification ### Artifacts Expected - `runs/kit/REQ-001/src/backend/db/migrations/versions/` — Alembic migration files - `runs/kit/REQ-001/src/backend/db/models/` — SQLAlchemy ORM model files - `runs/kit/REQ-001/test/backend/db/` — migration and model tests - `runs/kit/REQ-001/reports/migration.txt` — Alembic upgrade output log - `/eval` normalizes: migration success/failure, model import success, constraint enforcement ### CLI Examples - **Local:** - `alembic upgrade head` (verify migration applies) - `alembic downgrade base && alembic upgrade head` (verify idempotency) - `pytest test/backend/db/ -v` - **Containerized:** - `docker compose run --rm backend alembic upgrade head` - `docker compose run --rm backend pytest test/backend/db/ -v` ### Default Gate Policy - **min coverage:** 0% (schema REQ; coverage measured by migration success, not line coverage) - **max criticals:** 0 - **fail conditions:** migration fails to apply; migration is not idempotent; FK constraint not enforced; enum values do not match SPEC; pgvector extension not available ### Lane-Specific Failure Modes - **pgvector extension not installed:** migration will fail on `CREATE EXTENSION vector`; ensure test DB image includes pgvector - **Enum type conflicts:** PostgreSQL enums are not easily alterable; define all values upfront in REQ-001 - **Alembic autogenerate drift:** autogenerated migrations may miss CHECK constraints or custom types; always review generated SQL - **Circular FK references:** avoid circular foreign keys between tables; use nullable FKs or separate join tables if needed - **Timestamp precision:** use `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` for all temporal columns ### Enterprise Runner Notes - **SonarQube:** SQL files can be imported for analysis if sqlfluff reports are generated - **GitHub Actions:** use testcontainers or `postgres:16` service container with pgvector extension - **Artifact fetch:** migration logs at `runs/kit/REQ-001/reports/migration.txt` ### TECH_CONSTRAINTS Integration - **Air-gap:** PostgreSQL and pgvector images from approved internal registry - **Registries:** `ankane/pgvector:pg16` or equivalent approved image - **Tokens and secrets:** database credentials via environment variables in CI; production via `SecretAdapter` - **Migration strategy:** Alembic as specified in TECH_CONSTRAINTS; no Flyway or raw SQL scripts END_FILE BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/js-ts.md ## Lane Guide — js-ts ### Purpose Frontend lane for the Next.js 14 operator dashboard, validation workflow UI, archive search, and AI query interface.
